In the press release, Senate Bill 175 was explained to: only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants. inputs.modified_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday requiring new registered voters to prove that they are United States citizens in order to cast a ballot in state elections. This is yet another attempt to erect barriers against immigrant communities and other marginalized groups who already face systemic discrimination and unequal access to documentation. Far from protecting democracy, it deepens structural inequality by targeting vulnerable populations and limiting their ability to participate fully in shaping policies that affect their lives and labor. We need institutional reforms that expand voting rights and combat historical exclusion, not measures that reinforce power imbalances under the guise of tradition.
